title: Why checkout cart-abandonment spiked to 71%
caption: Root-cause analysis, 6M framework. Source: Q2 funnel + session-replay audit, n=2,140 abandoned sessions.

causes.text: Shipping cost shown only at end

semantic_description.level_1_elemental: Fishbone (Ishikawa) cause-and-effect diagram using the 6M framework. The fish head states the effect 'checkout cart-abandonment spiked from 58% to 71% in Q2'; six diagonal category ribs (Method, Machine, Material, Measurement, Manpower, Environment) branch off a central horizontal spine, each carrying 1-2 contributing causes with selected 5-whys sub-causes.
semantic_description.level_2_statistical: Six categories hold 11 first-level causes total; Method, Machine, and Material are the densest (2 causes plus a drilled sub-cause each). Tree depth reaches 3 (category to cause to sub-cause). The diagram is acyclic with no feedback edges.
semantic_description.level_3_perceptual: Causes cluster around a single mechanism: friction and cost surprises late in the flow (Method) compounded by a latency regression and stale-inventory errors (Machine, Material) that fail buyers at the payment step. Measurement gaps explain why the spike went undetected. Environment causes are external and not directly fixable.
semantic_description.level_4_contextual: The actionable cluster is the synchronous fraud-scoring call and the forced account creation; both are reversible engineering changes, unlike the competitor promo and the Safari autofill deprecation.
semantic_description.short_alt: Fishbone (6M) of a checkout abandonment spike to 71%, with late-flow friction and a payment-latency regression as densest causes.
